# BloodBridge – Database Design

## Part 3 – Constraints, Indexes & Database Standards

---

# 19. Primary Keys

Every table uses a single primary key.

| Table           | Primary Key |
| --------------- | ----------- |
| admin           | id          |
| camp            | id          |
| medical_partner | id          |
| team            | id          |
| volunteer       | id          |
| donor           | id          |
| screening       | id          |
| donation        | id          |

Primary keys are:

* Auto-generated
* BIGSERIAL
* Unique
* Never modified

---

# 20. Foreign Keys

| Child Table     | Foreign Key        | Parent Table    |
| --------------- | ------------------ | --------------- |
| medical_partner | camp_id            | camp            |
| team            | camp_id            | camp            |
| team            | medical_partner_id | medical_partner |
| volunteer       | team_id            | team            |
| donor           | camp_id            | camp            |
| screening       | donor_id           | donor           |
| screening       | volunteer_id       | volunteer       |
| donation        | donor_id           | donor           |
| donation        | volunteer_id       | volunteer       |

---

# 21. Unique Constraints

The following values must remain unique.

| Table     | Column          |
| --------- | --------------- |
| admin     | email           |
| donor     | registration_id |
| donor     | phone_number    |
| screening | donor_id        |
| donation  | donor_id        |

---

# 22. Indexes

To improve performance, indexes will be created on frequently searched fields.

## Donor

* registration_id
* phone_number
* full_name
* status

---

## Volunteer

* team_id

---

## Team

* medical_partner_id

---

## Screening

* donor_id

---

## Donation

* donor_id

---

# 23. Cascade Rules

Deleting important records should not accidentally remove historical data.

## Camp

Deletion is not allowed once registrations exist.

The camp should be archived instead.

---

## Donor

Deleting donors is not recommended.

Donor records should remain for reporting purposes.

---

## Team

Teams should not be deleted if volunteers exist.

Inactive teams should be marked as inactive.

---

## Volunteer

Volunteers should not be deleted.

Instead:

Status = INACTIVE

---

## Screening

Cannot exist without a donor.

---

## Donation

Cannot exist without a donor.

---

# 24. Enum Values

The application should use enums instead of storing random strings.

## Donor Status

* REGISTERED
* CHECKED_IN
* SCREENING
* APPROVED
* REJECTED
* COMPLETED
* NO_SHOW

---

## Team Status

* ACTIVE
* INACTIVE

---

## Camp Status

* UPCOMING
* ACTIVE
* COMPLETED
* ARCHIVED

---

## Gender

* MALE
* FEMALE
* OTHER

---

## Blood Quantity

Standard values:

* 350 ml
* 450 ml

---

# 25. Timestamp Fields

The following conventions shall be followed.

## created_at

Automatically set when a record is created.

---

## updated_at

Automatically updated whenever the record changes.

---

## screened_at

Automatically set when screening is saved.

---

## completed_at

Automatically set when donation is completed.

---

# 26. Database Rules

The following rules apply to all tables.

* Use BIGSERIAL for primary keys.
* Use foreign keys for relationships.
* Avoid duplicate data.
* Do not store calculated values (e.g., age).
* Use enums instead of hardcoded strings.
* Keep nullable fields to a minimum.
* Store timestamps using the server time.
* Do not expose internal IDs to users.

---

# 27. Final Database Structure

```text
camp
│
├── medical_partner
│        │
│        └── team
│               │
│               └── volunteer
│
└── donor
         │
         ├── screening
         └── donation
```

---

# 28. Database Summary

Database Engine

* PostgreSQL

Number of Tables

* 8

Main Entities

* Admin
* Camp
* Medical Partner
* Team
* Volunteer
* Donor
* Screening
* Donation

Design Principles

* Normalized structure
* Foreign key relationships
* Feature-oriented design
* Optimized for 1000–2000 donors
* Mobile and desktop ready
* Production-ready architecture

---

# Document Completion

This document defines the complete database architecture for BloodBridge Version 1.

All backend entities, repositories, database migrations, and SQL scripts shall follow this design.

Any future database modifications should be reflected in this document before implementation.
